Goa Power Sector Review 2024

Executive summary

The review assesses how the state's power sector can meet rising demand at lower cost and with lower emissions. Peak demand reached 815 MW in 2023 and is projected to exceed 1,200 MW by 2030. Goa buys about three quarters of its electricity from central and inter-state sources, most of it generated from coal. Studies show that coal prices will rise sharply. The MoP has asked all states to plan for a massive increase in demand. We find that Goa can meet half of its new demand locally by 2030. Rooftop and floating solar can supply about 350 MW, battery storage can shift midday output to the evening peak, and demand-side management (DSM) can save a further 60 MW. The total investment needed is about ₹4,800 crore over seven years. The state government would need to carry out an evaluation of each project before approval. Undoubtedly, the benefits will outweigh the costs. The state refused raising tariffs in 2023, and the cost and timing of new plants depends on the budget. The state must publish their progress report every year. The state should also expand demand-side management (DSM) to large hotels.

Three actions matter most. First, the government should set a target for local generation and publish an annual progress report. Second, it should reform the Net-Metering rules so that households and businesses can export surplus power at a fair price, and the net-metering rules should also cover housing societies. Third, it should tender 100 MW of battery storage by 2026. Each action is within the powers of the state and needs no change in central law
